chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked him about a man who owed me one hundred dirhams by count, and he paid me one hundred dirhams by weight. He said: 'There is no objection to it, provided there was no condition.' He also said: 'Usury arises from the condition, and it is the conditions that corrupt it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a debt counted in coins with the same weight in coins, and what makes it usury arise in this context?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies that repaying a counted debt with weighed currency is valid provided no specific condition (*shart*) is attached that introduces uncertainty or usury. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that *riba* in such exchanges often stems from contractual stipulations rather than the mere difference in measurement units, distinguishing between permissible variance and prohibited exploitation.
